The global shift to renewables is essential- but it must also be equitable. Cobalt and lithium are critical to clean technologies, yet their extraction often harms people and ecosystems. By 2050, the world will need 3x more cobalt and up to 40x lithium (compared to 2020 levels) driven by the needs of batteries, solar, wind, data centres and EVs .

In the DRC, which supplies over 70% of global cobalt, mining has polluted rivers, harmed crops and triggered human rights abuses -  including child labor. In Chile’s Atacama Desert, lithium operations have cut freshwater availability by 65%, threatening biodiversity and Indigenous livelihoods. 

This raises a critical question: how can we transition to a low-carbon future without deepening the nature and inequality crises? To ensure the clean energy transition is also a just transition, we must adopt integrated system-level solutions:

🔁 Closed-loop material systems can help reduce new extraction. Currently, only 1% of lithium and < 5% of cobalt is recycled from end-of-life batteries. Circular economy models - from battery reuse to advanced recycling - are essential to reduce demand for virgin mining.

🌍 Local value additions must be prioritized. Despite holding over half of global cobalt and manganese reserves,  Africa captures <5% of the global battery value chain. With battery demand set to triple by 2030, countries with an abundance of critical minerals should not be confined to raw extraction alone. By investing in local refining, battery production and and knowledge transfer, these countries can generate jobs, retain more economic value and reduce export dependency.

⚡ Smarter, greener grids are also important. Renewable energy sources are inherently variable. Next-generation energy efficient grids, such as AI-powered smart grids, can help balance supply and demand more effectively, reducing energy waste and integrating diverse power sources at scale.

The energy transition offers a once-in-a-generation opportunity to tackle climate change but only if it’s done in a way that is fair, inclusive and sustainable.
